card.name: Kagura
card.era: Ancient mythological origin (Ame-no-Uzume myth); codified from the Heian period onward
card.tagline: Sacred Shinto ceremonial dance offered to the kami
card.profile: Kagura ('god-entertainment') is a type of Shinto ritual ceremonial dance and music; the term contracts kami no kura ('seat of god'), indicating the presence of deities in the practice (Wikipedia). A major function is chinkon, the purifying and pacifying of the spirit (Wikipedia). According to the Kojiki and Nihon Shoki, its origin lies in the myth of Ame-no-Uzume, whose dance lured the sun goddess Amaterasu from her cave (Britannica). Two broad forms exist: mikagura, performed at the imperial court and major shrines such as Kamo and Iwashimizu Hachiman-gu, and satokagura, the folk variants including Iwami Kagura and Takachiho Kagura (Wikipedia).
card.insight: Kagura is treated as a sacred art dedicated to the kami; scholars hold it predates and influenced Noh theatre, especially in its storytelling and reenactment forms (Wikipedia).
